Q1.question: Is it sports-science acceptable that, when a review carries a clinical signal its handler's own screen routes to a human, the plan is not re-planned from that review's factual correction until the human route resolves, where FREEZE-2 proposed that re-plan alongside a nonclinical question?
Q1.answer: YES. R7-B.2's behaviour is required, and FREEZE-2's was the defect.
evidence: Reproduced S5R2 and S5R8 (out/s5-factual-proposal.json, identical to the Engineering record). FREEZE-2 returns ASK about the report id (S5R8: about the block choice) with proposal 439a61ba5e87c7206a79460c79594d857d33ddd746b52f8157aa37b9d0951240 and pending ASK. R7-B.2 returns 'The interruption reason is clinical or possibly clinical (flu, illness): qualified assessment is needed; no nonclinical return recipe', CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED, proposal null, pending CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED.

What the case is (out/week4-context.json, out/q3-resolution.json): the resend under the return's own id restates the week-3 interruption as 'Flu illness', and the correction restates week 4 (the first week after the return, at one set per exercise, RIR 3) with performance UNDER, recovery ADVERSE, effort HARDER and next-day function IMPAIRED. That is suspected illness with a new functional limitation on return, which SSCTR-05 and G04 assign to CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED, and which D08 already routes ('Flu illness' routes to clinical).

What the athlete is prescribed in weeks 5-11 while the route is pending. FREEZE-2: the re-planned program (week 5 strength cut from 3x12@20 / 3x8@22 / 2x10@22 to 2x10@20 / 2x8@22 / 1x10@22, runs unchanged), offered with a bookkeeping question, and the illness is not carried: the next review carrying FREEZE-2's reference state returns KEEP with no clinical dependency (q3 A/F1). That is a reduced dose offered in place of referral, which SSCTR-05 forbids ('do not suggest a dose or generic deload as a substitute for referral'). R7-B.2: no new prescription; plan validity REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION; the dependency is sticky (q3 A/F1 on R7-B.2: CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED, 'A prior clinical dependency remains outside this nonclinical reference; no automatic clearance', no proposal). The rows already in the program are not re-authorized by the runtime while the route is pending.

Consistency: B0-C06 condition 8 ('passes the clinical screen first: pain, injury, illness or a functional limitation routes CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED for the dependent scope'); D08; QE-R7B1-01 (a clinical route the handler takes is the decision, with no proposal); withFactualReplan ('A clinical route proposes nothing (no dependent prescription)'). For an illness return the dependent scope is the whole return, so withholding the whole re-plan is the correct scope.

The predecessor already decided exactly this for the same facts sent under a new id (S5R4, q3 path C) and for substitution pain with the same correction (S5R5, q3 path D): CLINICAL, no proposal, on both runtimes. R7-B.2's output for QE-R7B2-01 equals the predecessor's own path C step by step: same reason, same week-5 rows, same weeks 5-11 after the week-5 review (q3 comparison).
Q1.counterargument_tested: FREEZE-2 looks more conservative (fewer sets). Rejected: conservative is not automatic reduction (SSCTR-04); the reduction is a dose substituted for referral, and FREEZE-2 also drops the clinical dependency. Under R7-B.2 the higher rows are not a prescription the runtime stands behind while the route is pending.
Q1.confidence: HIGH for the routing judgment (it follows binding rules and is reproduced); individual clinical status is OUT_OF_SCOPE_CLINICAL

Q3.question: Is the factual correction's effect only deferred, not lost?
Q3.answer: Deferred, and carried into the next whole-week review; but for the rest of the current week it is not re-planned once the clinical dependency is no longer carried. This behaviour pre-exists B.2 and is identical on FREEZE-2 for the same facts under a new id and for substitution pain. Recorded as SSCTR-R7B2-01 (MINOR, routed, not blocking); not a correction-cycle item.
what_i_checked: The correction is recorded: actualLedger after the clinical route carries the corrections and supersedes the originals (q3 A ledgerHasCorrection true; S5R2 ledgerHasCorrection true).
While pending (reference state carried): sticky CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED, no proposal (q3 A/F1 on R7-B.2; also C, D on both runtimes).

Resolution as the runtime defines it: there is no clinical clearance path in evaluateProgram (by design: no AI clearance); the only continuation is a later review admitted without the carried pending state. The probes use that reading.

After that, a later review of the same week, with no reports (F2), with the same correction rows sent again (F3), or with a correction of the correction carrying identical facts (F4): KEEP, no proposal, on R7-B.2 path A and on both runtimes for paths C and D. The week-5 rows stay as planned before the correction (goblet squat 3x12@20; db-bench-press, db-row, db-rdl 3x8@22; db-split-squat 2x10@22; calf raise and dead bug 2 sets), where the correction applied at once gives one set fewer on each and goblet squat 2x10@20 (q3 E). The cause: the factual re-plan fires only on a review whose own reports move this week's PlanningView (viewMovedBy), and the correction is already in the carried record.

At the next whole-week review (week 5 executed and reviewed), the correction is read: weeks 6-8 differ from the same path without the correction (q3 A vs B, A vs F), and week 6 carries the corrected volume (2 sets per main exercise, against 3 without the correction). It is not lost from the plan ahead.

Late evidence (K6) after the clinical route: a later review with no signal and no reference state gets R7-A's question again, with the late report still recorded (q4 K6-after), identical on both runtimes.
Q3.acceptability: Acceptable for this gate. Withholding while pending is required (Q1). The remainder-of-week gap is pre-existing, bounded to one week, reachable only after the clinical dependency stops being carried (which the runtime itself never authorizes), keeps rows the approved rule produced from the facts as first reported, and is not a bypass of clinical-screen-first. Closing it narrowly would mean either attaching a dose to a clinical route (forbidden: QE-R7ADA-01, SSCTR-05) or changing the factual re-plan's trigger semantics shared with the predecessor's paths C and D (an R7-A / state-model change; contract stop conditions). So it is routed, not corrected in U5.

Q4.question: Same class elsewhere: S5b, S5c, S5f, S5h, S5R3, the K6/K6b rows and the CAND-01/CAND-02 rows.
Q4.answer: No sports-science concern. Each replaced question was nonclinical bookkeeping or scheduling, and none carried a proposal on either side; the clinical route is at least as restrictive (it proposes nothing either) and adds the referral and the sticky dependency that B0-C06 condition 8 and D08 require.
evidence: s5-factual-proposal: S5b, S5c, S5f, S5h, S5R3 go from ASK (no proposal) to CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED (no proposal).

q4-other-rows (mine): K6 pain, injury, clinical text, pain + ladder choice, pain + unrecognised choice: ASK (missing interruption.episodeId or choices) to CLINICAL, no proposal on either side, late report recorded. K6b step 2 (pain only, carrying step 1's state): ASK to CLINICAL, late report recorded. CAND-02 same id with illness, INJURY category or clinical flag: ASK (missing event.id) to CLINICAL. CAND-01 (state built as in the mission inventory) pain or illness with the correction: ASK (missing event.date) to CLINICAL, correction recorded.

Nothing nonclinical is lost: R7-A's late-evidence question returns on a later review without a clinical signal or pending state (K6-after, identical on both runtimes); the same-id nonclinical controls still get the id question; the CAND-01 weekly control still gets the factual question.

The only other differing row (CAND-02-after, carrying the reference state) differs because the carried state is now correctly clinical; the unchanged sticky rule then keeps the dependency. For the same input both runtimes decide alike (U3 carried-state check), and it is not a different decision rule.

Scope: for substitution pain the route is scoped to the named exercise (B0-C06 condition 8, 'for the dependent scope'), and the sticky state holds later reviews while it is carried. Identical to the predecessor's handling of the same report without late evidence (S5d, S5R5).

findings.title: A correction recorded by a clinically routed review is applied only at the next whole-week review
findings.statement: Once a later review is admitted without the pending clinical state, no review of the same week re-plans the sessions still ahead from a correction that a clinically routed review recorded. The correction is read when the week's whole-week review plans the following week.
findings.origin: Pre-existing. Residual authority closure QE-R7ADA-01 (withFactualReplan: a clinical route proposes nothing), combined with the decision-authority closure's factual re-plan trigger (viewMovedBy, Property B: only a review whose own reports move this week's PlanningView re-plans). Identical on R7B1-FREEZE-2 for the same facts under a new id and for substitution pain with the same correction. B.2 extends its reach to the same-id resend (QE-R7B2-01) and the re-entry clinical rows; the B.2 rule itself introduces no new mechanism.
findings.reproduction: probes/r1/q3-resolution.mjs: paths A (R7-B.2), C and D (both runtimes), follow-ups F2, F3, F4 all KEEP with no proposal; week-5 rows unchanged; weeks 6-8 differ between A and B after the week-5 review.
findings.consequence: For the remainder of that week, after the dependency stops being carried, the rows planned from the facts as first reported stay: here one more set per strength exercise at RIR 3, same loads, and goblet squat 3x12@20 instead of 2x10@20. Logs of that remainder are judged against rows planned from facts that no longer stand, which the factual re-plan exists to avoid (A1, D44 intent). Runs are unaffected.
findings.why_not_blocking: Pre-existing outside the QE-R7B1-04 class and not a safety bypass of the same invariant (contract §10). The clinical screen fires and nothing is proposed while it is carried. The kept rows are approved-rule outputs, bounded to one week, reachable only after an external resolution the runtime does not define. Under my standing criterion it is a deviation from a stricter rule whose prescription stays inside an approved envelope.
findings.not_a_U5_item: A narrow fix would either attach a dose to a clinical route (forbidden) or change the factual re-plan trigger shared with the predecessor's own clinical paths (R7-A / state model: contract stop conditions).
findings.owner: Next runtime mission (Engineering), with SSCTR for the dose reading and Data for the state semantics
findings.next_action: Decide how corrections recorded under a clinical route re-enter the planning of the sessions still ahead when a review is next admitted without a pending clinical dependency, without attaching anything to the clinical route itself.

findings.title: No runtime input represents a human resolution of a clinical dependency
findings.statement: evaluateProgram has no clearance path (correctly: no AI clearance). The only continuation is a review admitted without the carried pending state, after which the runtime has no record of the clinical reason: a clinical route records nothing in the program (q4 CAND-02-after without the reference state: KEEP on both runtimes; q3 F2). What a documented human resolution looks like as an input, and what the nonclinical continuation then starts from, is undefined.
findings.origin: Pre-existing (R6 reference continuation state and the clinical boundary design); identical on both runtimes.
findings.owner: Founder/Product (service model) with Engineering (input contract) and the qualified-human clinical route; SSCTR only for the nonclinical continuation after a documented human resolution
findings.next_action: Define the input by which a documented human resolution re-enters, without any agent clearance or new clinical reading.
